<explanation>
Below is a step-by-step guide for creating a system design diagram tailored to the WeatherStar 4000+ project. Use this to communicate the architecture clearly to other engineers.

1. Identify Project Type and Purpose  
   - This is a full-stack, Node.js-based web application that simulates a “90’s Weather Channel” local forecast using modern HTML/CSS/JS.  
   - The Node server (index.mjs) serves dynamic views (EJS), static assets, and acts as a CORS proxy to NOAA’s Weather API.

2. Analyze the File Structure  
   • Root  
     – index.mjs: entry point, starts Node server  
     – Dockerfile / .github/workflows: CI/CD & containerization  
     – gulpfile.mjs + gulp/**: build pipeline for static distribution (/dist)  
   • server/  
     – scripts/: CORS proxy modules + optional custom.js hook  
     – fonts/, images/, music/: static assets served to client  
     – styles/: SCSS & compiled CSS for styling  
     – manifest.json, robots.txt: PWA config & crawler hints  
   • views/  
     – index.ejs + partials/: server-side templates build the UI shell  
   • src/, cors/, datagenerators/:  
     – src/: auxiliary scripts (playlist generation)  
     – cors/: static CORS proxies usable in serverless setups  
     – datagenerators/: offline data‐preparation scripts  
   • dist/: final static bundle for CDN/S3 hosting  
   • tests/: unit & integration tests  

3. Key Insights from README  
   - Node server solves CORS by proxying api.weather.gov requests.  
   - Build step (`npm run buildDist`) emits `/dist` for pure-static deployment.  
   - Uses ES modules, classes, async/await, Luxon date library.  
   - UI is rendered in EJS, then enhanced by client-side JS modules (under server/scripts/modules).  

4. Main Components & Their Interactions  
   a. Browser (Client)  
     • Loads HTML from Node server (EJS).  
     • Fetches CSS/JS static assets.  
     • Invokes client modules to render each “display.”  
     • Makes API calls to CORS proxy endpoints on the Node server.  
   b. Node.js Server  
     • HTTP server (index.mjs) using native http or Express-like routing.  
     • Serves EJS templates and static folders (styles, images, music).  
     • Implements CORS proxy routes (server/scripts/modules/utils/cors.mjs).  
     • Hosts custom hook (server/scripts/custom.js).  
   c. NOAA Weather API (external)  
     • Authoritative data source for all weather data via REST.  
     • Node server proxies requests, adds CORS headers.  
   d. Build System (Gulp)  
     • Runs tasks: compile SCSS → CSS, bundle or copy JS, optimize assets.  
     • Outputs fully static site under /dist.  
   e. Optional Data‐Generation Scripts (offline)  
     • datagenerators/*.mjs produce JSON used in tests or demos.  

5. Architectural Patterns & Principles  
   - Separation of concerns: UI (EJS + CSS), data fetching/proxy (server scripts), build pipeline.  
   - Modular client-side code: each display is an ES6 class under server/scripts/modules.  
   - Proxy pattern for CORS (single point of entry for external API).  
   - Static site export capability for CDN hosting (serverless).  
   - Containerization via Docker for easy local run & CORS handling.  

6. How to Lay Out Your Diagram  
   - Draw 4 main boxes:  
     1. Client Browser  
     2. Node.js Server  
     3. NOAA Weather API (external)  
     4. Build System / CI & CD (Gulp, Docker, GitHub Actions)  
   - Within the Node.js Server box, subdivide into:  
     • EJS View Engine → views/partials  
     • Static Asset Server → styles/, images/, music/  
     • CORS Proxy Module → server/scripts/modules/utils/cors.mjs  
     • Customization Hook → server/scripts/custom.js  
   - Show arrows:  
     • Browser → GET / → Node  
     • Browser → GET /scripts, /styles → Node static server  
     • Browser → XHR /cors/* → Node CORS proxy  
     • Node CORS proxy → HTTPS → NOAA API  
     • Gulp (build) → outputs /dist → possible static hosting/CDN  
     • GitHub Actions → Docker build & push → container registry  
   - Use color coding / shapes:  
     • Blue rectangles for internal components (View Engine, CORS Module)  
     • Green for external (NOAA API, CDN)  
     • Orange for build/CI (Gulp, GitHub Actions, Docker)  

7. Tailoring Guidelines  
   - Emphasize separation of server-rendered templates vs. static hosting: show two deployment modes (Node server vs. fully static).  
   - Highlight the proxy pattern for CORS: a central module through which all weather data flows.  
   - Call out the modular client‐side display classes: each EJS partial invokes a JS class.  
   - Show testing infrastructure (tests/), if you want to illustrate CI coverage.  

8. Diagram Elements Checklist  
   – Clear, descriptive labels on every box.  
   – Directional arrows with method/type (e.g., GET, XHR).  
   – Legend explaining colors/shapes.  
   – Annotations for build outputs (/dist) and deployment targets (Docker container, S3).  

By following these steps and visual groupings, you’ll capture the essential architecture of WeatherStar 4000+—its data flows, build pipeline, and runtime components—without overcomplicating the diagram.
